To fix schema drift in your project, you need to perform a full database reset. This process will drop the database/schema (if possible), recreate it, apply all migrations, and run seed scripts. Here's how you can do it:

1. Make sure you are in the root directory of your project.
2. Run the following command:

```
npx prisma migrate reset --force
```

This command will reset your database and migration history, ensuring that your database schema matches your Prisma schema. Please note that this should only be done on a development database and not on a production database. If you have any important data that you need to preserve, make sure to back it up before running this command.

To delete an old development database, you can use the `migrate-reset` command with the `--force` flag. This will reset the database and migration history, effectively deleting the old database and starting fresh. Here's how you can do it:

1. Make sure you are in the root directory of your project.
2. Run the following command:

```bash
prisma migrate reset --force
```

This command will drop the database (if possible), recreate it, apply all migrations, and run any seed scripts. Please note that this action is irreversible, so ensure that you do not need any data from the current database before proceeding.

1. Open your terminal or command prompt.

3. Run the following command:

```

```
